transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just weren’t here anymore, and these thoughts about not wanting to wake up won’t stop. A colleague of mine insisted that I come in to get some help, so I'm here.
I am so sorry you are going through this. Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life recently?

Yes, they did. About a year and a few months ago, my father passed away unexpectedly from a heart attack in Indonesia, and I wasn't able to travel back for his funeral due to visa issues and work coverage. The heavy grief and guilt of not being there for my family started this entire downward spiral.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, active, and needing very little sleep for days at a time?
No, I've never experienced periods like that where I felt unusually energetic or hyperactive. My struggle has really only been the opposite—feeling extremely down, empty, and heavy.
Before your father passed away, have you ever experienced other periods in your life where you felt this same kind of deep sadness or emptiness for weeks at a time?
No, I have never experienced this kind of deep sadness or emptiness before my father passed away. This is the first time in my life that I have ever felt this way.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before your father passed away?

Yes, completely. I used to look forward to hiking, photography, and trying new recipes, but now those things feel entirely flat and pointless. Most days I just end up sitting in my apartment staring at the wall or mindlessly scrolling through my phone.
Have these feelings of deep sadness, lack of interest, and thoughts about not wanting to wake up been present nearly every day for at least the past two weeks?

Yes, I feel this way almost every single day. It has been going on for much longer than just two weeks, though—it's been a constant, heavy weight for a little over a year now, ever since the months after my father passed.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as having trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping too much?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns. My mind is usually so focused on other overwhelming thoughts that I honestly haven't paid much attention to how I'm sleeping.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight since this downward spiral began, such as eating much less or more than usual?
To be honest, I haven't really paid attention to my appetite or weight. Everything else has been so overwhelming that I'm just not sure if there have been any changes.
Have you been feeling an overwhelming lack of energy or physical exhaustion, making even simple daily tasks feel like a huge effort?

Yes, my body constantly feels incredibly heavy, as if I am trying to move through wet cement just to walk from my car to the clinic. Because even the simplest tasks take so much effort, basic daily chores like cooking, laundry, and cleaning have completely fallen apart at home.
Have you been having trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions since this downward spiral began?

Yes, my concentration has been terrible lately. On rounds, I find myself reading the same line in a patient's chart over and over without actually absorbing any of the information. Even simple everyday decisions, like choosing what to eat for lunch, can take me ten minutes because my mind feels so foggy.
Aside from the guilt about not being there for your father's funeral, have you been experiencing strong feelings of worthlessness or blaming yourself for other things?

Yes, most days I feel like a fraud who doesn't deserve to be a doctor or even a son. I get stuck replaying every missed phone call to my dad and every minor error at work, convinced that I'm a fundamentally bad person who deserves to be punished for all the harm I've caused.
Did these difficult feelings and symptoms first begin within three months of your father's passing, or did they start later than that?
Yes, they started within the first couple of months after his passing. The heavy grief and guilt over not being there for my family began building up almost immediately during that initial period.
